title: AlternatePlans 1.0: the other things worth testing, as experiments
description: A run surfaces more good ideas than one round can test -- a Notch ligand, a surfactant load, GM-CSF as a timed surge rather than a constant -- and they end up as prose in a report nobody turns into an experiment. This is where a person's pick of them becomes testable: each one a claim, the arms that would settle it, what it would cost to run, and what they would do with either outcome. Written by the orchestrator from what the run already read, at the person's request, in their words. Two things it may never do: change the main hypothesis, and change round 1. Round 1's rules were fixed before any result existed and its commitment digest says so; an alternate that could rewrite it would make that promise worthless. These sit beside it, labelled proposed, for a person to choose from.

request.description: What the person asked for, in their own words, kept as data.

relation.description: alternate: a different way to reach the same objective. extension: the main hypothesis plus this, tested on top of it.

claim.description: What would be true if it holds. A claim, not a topic.

rationale.description: What in this run's evidence makes it worth a vessel.

differs_from_main.description: How this differs from the main hypothesis. An alternate that is the main one restated wastes a vessel.

registered.description: Whether the project has this parameter. Filled by BioSense.

on_top_of.description: The round-1 arm this one is run on top of, for an extension.

evidence_basis.description: cited: sources test this. mechanistic: sources support the mechanism, not this change. judgement: the orchestrator's own reasoning, which caps confidence at low.

would_change.description: What changes about the recommendation if it holds.

cost.description: What running it actually costs: vessels, a construct, a reagent nobody has, an extra week.

not_pursued.description: Things the person asked about that did not become a plan, and why.
